summary.headline: Waaree FY26 revenue rose ~84% to INR26,537 crore and operating EBITDA 117% to INR5,909 crore, but Q4 margin fell to ~18.6% on commodity, freight and mix pressures.
summary.overview: FY26 was a record year: revenue from operations of INR26,537 crore (+84% YoY), operating EBITDA of INR5,909 crore (22.27% margin vs 18.84%) and PAT of INR3,884 crore (+101%). Q4 revenue was INR8,480 crore (+111% YoY) and operating EBITDA INR1,576 crore, with margin down sharply from the prior quarter as silver and copper costs, freight spikes, lower overseas mix and in-house DCR cell shortfall weighed. Management guided FY27 operating EBITDA to INR7,000-7,700 crore and framed the Waaree 2.0 capex (~$3.5 billion) as the driver, with most cell and module capex completing in FY27 and benefits from H2 FY27 onward. Operating cash conversion fell to about 27% as export shipments were stuck on logistics delays and inventory built up.

segments.name: Module manufacturing
segments.commentary: FY26 production 12.6 GW (+77%), sales about 12 GW; Q4 production 4.2 GW (+104% YoY) and Q4 sales 4.1 GW. Capacity ~26 GW, described as the largest non-Chinese module maker.

segments.name: Cell manufacturing
segments.commentary: Operational cell capacity 5.4 GW (largest in India); Q4 cell production 0.7 GW. A 10 GW cell facility is due in H2 FY27, taking cell capacity to ~15.4 GW.

segments.name: Revenue mix (FY26)
segments.commentary: Utility/IPP/C&I 34.7%, overseas 33%, retail 20.8%, EPC 11.6%. Retail revenue INR5,515 crore (+84%). Q4 overseas share fell to ~21% from ~32% in Q3.

segments.name: US manufacturing
segments.commentary: 1.6 GW plant ramped; 2.6 GW more to go live within six months, taking US capacity to 4.2 GW. IRA benefit ~$0.07/Wp, ~$40 million in FY26, to rise with new capacity.

segments.name: Order book
segments.commentary: ~INR53,000 crore excluding retail (~20% of revenue), up from ~INR47,000 crore a year ago but down ~INR7,000 crore QoQ per analyst. ~65-70% is overseas, to be delivered over 3-4 years. More than INR8,400 crore delivered already.

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating EBITDA guided at INR7,000-7,700 crore (about 20-25% growth on FY26 INR5,909 crore).
Management says the margin benefit from in-house DCR cells starts in H2 FY27 when the 10 GW cell line goes live; H1 is a transition.
Long-range planning assumption: 19-20% EBITDA margin sustained for a decade.
Cell utilisation assumed 80-85% for FY28 on 15.4 GW capacity; 28 GW modules, 4 GW inverters, 20,000 MVA transformers and 1 GW electrolyser to run at full throttle in FY28.
Capex of ~$3.5 billion (INR30,000 crore) over the next two years; core module and cell capex complete in FY27, ingot wafer and part of battery in FY28; full Waaree 2.0 benefits seen in FY29.
Cell line transition from M10R to G12R expected to lift output and realisation by 10-12% within about a quarter; module output back to ~330 MW a month within two months.
Investor Day to be held; enabling board resolution for fundraise of up to ~INR10,000 crore approved, with shareholder approval to follow.
capex_capacity: Battery (BESS): 20 GWh planned, phase 1 of 3.5 GWh in FY27 (Gujarat), phase 2 of 16.5 GWh in FY28; capex ~INR10,000 crore.
Ingot wafer: 10 GW at Nagpur, capex ~INR6,200 crore (up from INR5,100 crore earlier with 6 GW to 10 GW); completion FY28.
PV glass: 2,500 TPD approved at ~INR3,900 crore capex, production expected within 24 months; supports ~16-17 GW of modules.
Inverters: 4 GW at Sarodhi, Gujarat (~INR180 crore); 3 GW commissioned, remaining 1 GW in FY27.
Transformers: current ~4,000 MVA; adding 16,000 MVA to reach 20,000 MVA at Alwar (~INR192 crore) in FY27.
Hydrogen: 1 GW electrolyser at Dungri, Gujarat (~INR676 crore capex); electrolyser PLI INR444 crore and hydrogen PLI ~INR510 crore.
Acquired ~55% of Associated Power Structures Ltd (APSL) for ~INR1,225 crore for T&D entry; Oman polysilicon stake acquired for non-Chinese supply.
Module lines: 3 lines converted to G12R (ramping), 3 lines remain Mono PERC, 5 lines still on M10R TOPCon, to convert over about one quarter.
demand_pricing: Domestic DCR module pricing INR21-22/Wp; non-DCR utility INR15-16/Wp, with retail carrying a premium; commodity increases are being passed through to new orders.
Silver and copper cost increases, freight spikes and a lower overseas share weighed on Q4 margin; management said customers are now accepting the higher commodity-linked prices.
ALMM-II (domestic cell mandate) takes effect June 2026; C&I and mid-market decisions were deferred pending clarity, which slowed local offtake.
India installed 44.6 GW of solar in FY26; module consumption was about 50-55 GW. Management sees DCR-compliant cell capacity at ~30 GW for ALMM-II.
US FEOC rules from April 2026 require non-Chinese cells and components, which management says is driving new US orders.
BESS pricing around $110-120/MWh cited for India and US; BESS margin guided at 18-20% before policy support.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating EBITDA margin fall sharply QoQ, and what are the DCR and non-DCR realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited silver and copper cost spikes, freight cost surge, a lower overseas mix and DCR cell shortfall. DCR modules INR21-22/Wp; utility non-DCR INR15-16/Wp, with a retail premium.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the export mix low in Q4 and what is the order book composition?
qa_highlights.answer: Export shipments were stuck on Middle East logistics delays, so inventory rose. About 65-70% of the INR53,000 crore order book is overseas, delivered over 3-4 years; retail (~20% of revenue) is excluded.

qa_highlights.question: How will the FY27 EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore be achieved, and what drives margin?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 is a transition from 5.4 GW to 15.4 GW of cells; the 10 GW cell line in H2 lifts in-house DCR supply. Pre-startup costs for new projects are included in guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the ingot-wafer capex rise and its timeline move to FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity was raised from 6 GW to 10 GW and sites moved from Odisha to Gujarat and Nagpur, causing the delay. The new figure covers the full 10 GW.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash conversion cycle and working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory built up because overseas shipments were delayed. Customer advances stayed steady but production nearly doubled, diluting working capital days. Management expects cash conversion of 70-100% at normalised inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What are the BESS unit economics and FY29 revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: BESS margin guided at 18-20% without policy support. Management declined to give FY29 revenue guidance, pointing to the 20 GWh capacity and $110-120/MWh pricing.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on the 10 GW cell line commissioning in H2 FY27 and on the G12R ramp; Q4 showed sharp margin compression.
Working capital and cash conversion (~27%) need to normalise as stuck export inventory ships.
ALMM-II timing uncertainty is deferring C&I and mid-market orders; order book fell ~INR7,000 crore QoQ.
Commodity (silver, copper) and freight volatility; pricing pass-through to new orders is unproven.
Execution risk on ~$3.5 billion capex across BESS, glass, ingot-wafer and US plants, plus fundraise of up to INR10,000 crore.
Overcapacity concerns in the module sector; management argues demand and supply balance once ALMM-II/III take effect.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the long-term Waaree 2.0 story and on FY26 results. Noticeably defensive and detailed when explaining the Q4 margin drop, cash conversion and order-book sequential decline, often attributing them to temporary logistics and transition factors. Several answers on BESS economics, the fundraise, Indosolar and ALMM-II timing were deferred or left unquantified.

financial_highlights.change: Above prior guidance of INR5,500-6,000 crore
+70% YoY; margin fell sharply QoQ (analyst cited ~590 bps decline)

key_quotes: Our capital allocation follows a simple principle, book and build, which means every rupee we deploy is backed by confirmed demand and a clear path to returns.
The safest assumption there will be is your 19 %-20% margin consistent for a decade long at least.
So, we really don't foresee any scenario anytime next 5, 10 years of time will be the supply is going to be much higher than demand.
So, if you keep the inventory at normalized levels, the same number will go back to the normalized level of 70% to 100% conversion of cash from current 27%.
